title: Encrypted DNS Discovery Advertisement Planning Architecture
purpose: Define the adapter-neutral router and forwarder advertisement planning boundary for RFC 9463 encrypted DNS discovery.
design_summary: The advertisement planner maps local router or forwarder configuration into DHCPv4 OPTION_V4_DNR, DHCPv6 OPTION_V6_DNR, and Neighbor Discovery encrypted DNS option payloads using the existing RFC 9463 codecs. It preserves service priority, lifetime, authentication domain name, default or supplied service parameters, address-family applicability, ADN-only publication, and non-ready statuses for no usable addresses or locally disabled advertisement surfaces.
data_and_state_considerations: The planner is side-effect free. It does not configure DHCP servers, send Router Advertisements, write platform network state, publish DNS provider records, or open encrypted DNS sessions.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Mixed IPv4 and IPv6 addresses produce DHCPv4, DHCPv6, and Router Advertisement payloads.
ADN-only publication produces address-free DHCPv4, DHCPv6, and Router Advertisement payloads when those surfaces are requested.
IPv4-only populated plans do not invent IPv6 DHCPv6 or Router Advertisement payloads.
Loopback or otherwise unusable resolver addresses produce a no-usable-addresses plan.
Disabling all publication surfaces produces a policy-blocked plan.
risks: The planner cannot verify that supplied addresses are actually LAN-facing interfaces on the host.
Actual DHCP server, router, and operating-system advertisement APIs remain platform-specific and outside this slice.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The artifact converts router and forwarder advertisement work into deterministic payload planning while keeping live platform emission and network-interface ownership external.
